Cook visited Apple's Battersea campus in London this week to meet with King Charles, as part of the company's new partnership with the King's Foundation.

At Apple's Battersea headquarters, Cook also sat down for an in-depth interview with The Independent, discussing the partnership and his first month as Apple's executive chairman.

Cook stepped down as Apple CEO last month, handing the reins over to John Ternus. In this week's interview, he revealed that the transition actually began "several years ago."

The first product launched after Ternus took over as CEO was the iPhone Duo, which Cook said had been planned well in advance. He explained: "I wanted John to ride a tailwind, and Apple's tailwind is very much about the product cycle."

Cook also emphasized that, in his role as executive chairman, he is focused on "global policy" work, noting that there is a "very high level of trust" between him and Ternus. Cook said he will assist Ternus "in any way he deems appropriate," but stressed that he "won't be micromanaging."

What advice did Cook give Ternus? "Don't try to be me." The full interview is available on The Independent, and includes a fascinating discussion about the new partnership with the King's Foundation.
